In addition, the Federal Reserve will announce its monetary policy decision on Wednesday. The market expects rates to stay in the 4.75%-4.00% range.

“The Fed won’t raise interest rates again when it meets this week, and it shouldn’t. The economy is threatened by a growing list of risks, and a Fed misstep is one of them,” said Mark Zandi, chief economist at Moodys Analytics.

“That’s the clear message in our risk matrix, which sizes up each risk by how likely it is to occur over the next 12 to 18 months and how much economic damage it would cause if it did. There’s a lot of red in the matrix, indicating risks that are becoming more likely or more severe,” Zandi said.

Lastly, the Chicago Fed National Activity Index rose in September, exceeding consensus and indicating increased economic growth compared with August’s reading.
